mechanism: Involuntary delisting from a listed US exchange to the Pink Sheets/OTC forces regulated institutional holders to sell regardless of price
forced_by: Regulated funds: 'SEC rules preclude most institutions from holding unlisted shares, thus forcing owners to move out of these shares' (Macey-O'Hara-Pompilio 2004 WP, footnote 45)
source: Macey, J., O'Hara, M., Pompilio, D., 'Down and Out in the Stock Market: The Law and Finance of the Delisting Process', working paper July 2004 (published as '...Law and Economics of the Delisting Process', Journal of Law and Economics 51(4) 683-713, 2008)
claimed_effect: Average close $0.95 last NYSE day -> $0.48 first Pink Sheet day ('being evicted reduces the stock's value by almost one-half'); 9 largest $0.57->$0.16; ex-bankruptcy $1.09->$0.59. $100 equal-weighted portfolio formed on first Pink Sheet day rises to almost +30% within the first ~30 trading days, then -20% by day 60
claimed_net_sharpe_or_t: none - the paper reports a cumulative portfolio path in a figure, no t-statistic on a return series and no Sharpe
derivation: not derivable; I decline to manufacture a Sharpe from a figure description
sample: 63 forced NYSE delistings in calendar year 2002; 57 moved to the Pink Sheets and form the trading sample. One year, one exchange, N=57
net_of_costs: NO - and the authors state the opposite: 'it is implausible that returns remain positive when overall trading costs are properly included'. Measured median spread 25% on day 1; 13.60%-14.93% at 60 days; spreads triple vs NYSE
bets_per_year: ~12 portfolio-level bets/yr at a 30-day hold. Universe: paper's own '7300 firms delisted since 1995, almost half involuntary' implies ~430 involuntary delistings/yr across all US markets (my calculation, 7300*0.5/8.5yr, order-of-magnitude only); NYSE alone 63 in 2002
decay_evidence: none reported, no follow-up found. Unverified structural change: SEC Rule 15c2-11 as amended Sept 2021 moved many non-reporting OTC names to the Expert Market
free_data_path: Alpaca /v2/assets (19,182 inactive US equities, ~2,867 inactive on listed exchanges) + Alpaca SIP daily bars 2016+ which do cover delisted names (verified 2026-09-11); SEC Form 25 / 25-NSE for the delisting date
missing_data: (a) post-delisting Pink Sheet/OTC bars - the trade happens entirely after the last listed bar and it is UNVERIFIED whether Alpaca returns anything there; (b) no OTC quote/spread data at all, so the 13-25% spread cannot be modelled; (c) EDGAR ingested for ~503 large caps only, so Form 25 dating needs a new roster
crit_i: YES - the source states the constraint as a legal one on holders who must exit an unlisted security
crit_ii: YES - the security leaves the listed venue, which is the exact exclusion that keeps large regulated capital out
strongest_anti_evidence: The authors' own sentence that costs make positive returns implausible, at a measured 25% median first-day spread; plus N=57 in one year and no net Sharpe of any kind
verdict: HOLD - do not build; run a 30-minute Alpaca probe for post-delisting bars first

mechanism: Open-end funds hit by redemptions must sell predetermined holdings; whoever warehouses the inventory demands a premium, largest where trading capacity is thin
forced_by: Open-end mutual funds facing investor redemptions (flow measure Eq. 34; FIT Eq. 35; ForcedSale Eq. 36)
source: Ziyao Wang, 'Residual Supply and the Price of Risk Absorption', arXiv:2605.30672v1 [q-fin.GN], 29 May 2026 - UNREFEREED PREPRINT, single author, Dept of Mathematics and Statistics, Texas Tech
claimed_effect: Table 8 (above-median fund exposure, dollar-volume split): AbsInv slopes 4.54/39.03/91.77 bp at 1/3/6m (t=0.22/0.74/0.93) high dollar volume vs 96.60/375.46/729.63 bp (t=2.06/3.79/5.14) low dollar volume. Table 9 portfolio sorts: no-microcap EW H-L 44.09 bp/mo (t=2.85); VALUE-weighted 20.92 bp/mo (t=1.29)
claimed_net_sharpe_or_t: 0.6076 GROSS annualized Sharpe from Table 9 EW H-L (t=2.85)
derivation: my calculation: SR_ann = t/sqrt(years) = 2.85/sqrt(22) = 0.6076; cross-check 264 months, monthly SR 2.85/sqrt(264)=0.17541, x sqrt(12) = 0.6076. Table 8's t=2.06 would give 0.4392 but it is a Fama-MacBeth rank-spread coefficient, not a tradable return; the 3m/6m t-stats use overlapping horizons and are not convertible
sample: US common stocks Jan 2003 - 2024 (22 years); 490,162 no-microcap stock-months, 5,559 PERMNOs
net_of_costs: NO - costs appear in the theory (Sec 2) but no net-of-cost return and no spread assumption is reported
decay_evidence: none reported. The paper does not cite Wardlaw (2020) at all (grep -c -i wardlaw = 0) despite building on the FIT measure Wardlaw's critique targets
free_data_path: SEC N-PORT bulk quarterly holdings 2019q4-2026q2 already downloaded (filtered to S&P 500/600 CUSIPs; full zips ~440MB/quarter, re-downloadable) + Alpaca daily bars
missing_data: CUSIP->ticker map for micro-caps (hardest gap: N-PORT gives CUSIP/ISIN/LEI, Alpaca gives tickers, no free crosswalk covers delisted microcaps); point-in-time market-cap history below the S&P 600 (needs a point-in-time share count we do not hold); N-PORT starts 2019q4 = 6.8 years, worsening the admissibility threshold
crit_i: YES - redemption-driven selling is mechanical and predetermined by lagged holdings
crit_ii: NO as published - Sec 3.1: the no-microcap sample 'keeps stocks with market equity above the 20th percentile of New York'. Every headline table excludes exactly the corner criterion (ii) requires
strongest_anti_evidence: Wardlaw (JF 2020): after removing the embedded realized return, outflows give 'a fairly negligible quarterly decline in returns, with no subsequent reversal' - the reversal is the trade. Also: the value-weighted version of this paper's own sort is insignificant (t=1.29), and coval_stafford_firesale already failed here because ownership breadth in S&P 500/600 was 643/246 owners per stock vs the paper's 47
verdict: DECLINE_AT_SOURCING - power (0.6076 gross vs a 2.416 net threshold) and economics (source excludes our corner)

mechanism: Annual Russell reconstitution forces index funds to buy additions and sell deletions on a published date
forced_by: Russell-index-tracking funds, by index rules; assignment is by end-of-May market-cap rank
source: Chang, Y., Hong, H., Liskovich, I., 'Regression Discontinuity and the Price Effects of Stock Market Indexing', NBER WP 19290, Aug 2013 (published Review of Financial Studies 28(1) 212-246, 2015)
claimed_effect: 1000 cut-off (1996-2012, bw 100, p=1): June addition +0.050 (t=2.65), deletion +0.054 (t=3.00); no May effect and no reversal in Jul-Sep. 3000 cut-off = the microcap boundary (2005-2012, bw 100): addition June +0.036 (t=1.45), deletion +0.033 (t=1.25) - BOTH INSIGNIFICANT
claimed_net_sharpe_or_t: not derivable - an RD coefficient on a June cross-section is not a return series
derivation: for scale only, my calculation: 2.65/sqrt(17)=0.643 (1000 cut-off) and 1.45/sqrt(8)=0.513 (3000 cut-off); both are meaningless as Sharpes (one observation per name per year) and are shown only to place them far below 2.416
sample: 1996-2012 at the 1000 cut-off; 2005-2012 at the 3000 cut-off (Russell 3000E does not exist before 2005). Table 8 N = 822-835 (addition), 764-771 (deletion) name-years
bets_per_year: 1 - a single reconstitution date per year (~100 names at the 3000 cut-off)
decay_evidence: Russell banding from the 2007 reconstitution cut index switching from ~10% of Russell 1000 firms/yr to ~3% (CHL Sec 2; Appel-Gormley-Keim Sec 2.2) - a ~70% reduction in forced trades. CHL state there is NO banding at the 3000 cut-off
missing_data: Russell constituent history (not held); Russell's end-of-May market cap is PROPRIETARY and unobservable - Appel-Gormley-Keim: with CRSP 2006 caps 'only 68% of the firms ranked between 950 and 1,000 were included in the Russell 1000', and Russell 'has been unwilling to share the historical market caps'; this project has no CRSP and no point-in-time share count
crit_i: YES - index funds are mandated to trade on the reconstitution date
crit_ii: NO - the reconstitution is the most heavily traded scheduled liquidity event in US equities; CHL note predicting switches 'represents a profitable trading opportunity' Russell may be deliberately obscuring
strongest_anti_evidence: CHL's own Table 8: t=1.45 and t=1.25 at the 3000 cut-off - insignificant exactly at the microcap boundary, while the famous 5% effect lives at the 1000 cut-off in $1bn+ names. Plus Appel-Gormley-Keim on unobservable assignment
verdict: DECLINE - insignificant in the corner, 1 bet/yr, not implementable on free data

mechanism: December tax-loss selling by taxable holders, concentrated in small/micro caps, reverses in January
forced_by: Taxable individual and institutional holders, by the US tax code - an incentive, not a mandate to trade on a date
source: not re-sourced from the literature; the deciding evidence is this project's own run (data/research_runs/dormant_pool_2026-09-09/POPULATE_REPORT.md)
claimed_effect: project's own: December specs +0.4965 (tax_loss_selling_turn_of_year/tls_dec_jul_dec_lossonly_h6, n=2932) and +0.4152 (small-cap twin, n=1677) net Sharpe
claimed_net_sharpe_or_t: n/a - the placebo defeats the claim before power matters
sample: project's own, n=2932 / n=1677 daily observations
free_data_path: already built and run in this project
crit_i: PARTLY - the tax code creates the incentive but compels nobody to trade on a date
strongest_anti_evidence: The JUNE PLACEBO beat the December spec: tls_jun_placebo_signed_h21 scored +0.5259 (n=2932) and +0.5343 (small-cap twin, n=1677) vs December's +0.4965 / +0.4152. Both families 'remain NOT PARKED on attribution grounds'. Shrinking the universe does not repair an attribution failure
verdict: DECLINE - already falsified on this project's own data

mechanism: SPAC common shares are redeemable at pro-rata trust value, so the downside is structurally floored by the trust
forced_by: The SPAC trust, by charter - it must pay pro-rata NAV on redemption
source: Gahng, Ritter & Zhang, 'SPACs', Review of Financial Studies 2023 - read and hashed on 2026-09-11, hunting_ground_review_2026-09-11/sources/gahng_ritter_zhang_spacs.txt; NOT re-sourced today
claimed_effect: Equal-weighted annualised SPAC-period return 23.9% over an average 16-month hold; liquidated SPACs still +2.0% annualised; the worst SPAC IPO in the sample +0.51% annualised
derivation: bets per year is mine: 458/11 = ~42 SPACs per year
net_of_costs: see the 2026-09-11 review; not re-checked today
bets_per_year: ~42 (my calculation, 458 over 11 years); issuance collapsed after 2022
decay_evidence: the authors' own warning: the excluded 2021 cohort (613 IPOs) 'appear to be producing annualized SPAC period returns in the low single digits'; the 2026-09-11 review also recorded the post-2022 collapse in issuance
crit_i: YES - the trust must redeem at NAV
crit_ii: PARTLY - the 15% redemption cap binds concerted large holders and not a small one
strongest_anti_evidence: The authors' own warning about the 2021 cohort, plus the bet count and the post-2022 collapse in SPAC issuance
verdict: ALREADY REVIEWED 2026-09-11 (hunting-ground rank 4); listed here only to complete the census of mandated-flow mechanisms
